plan.planning_summary: This portfolio tests three genuinely distinct strategy axes for a solar-blind UV bandpass filter: (1) material pair selection between HfO2/SiO2 and Al2O3/MgF2, which have different UV transparency and index contrast; (2) stack topology between a simple periodic Bragg reflector with single cavity versus a multi-cavity defect structure for sharper passband; (3) thickness distribution strategy between uniform quarter-wave pairs versus chirped periods for broader blocking. These axes can disagree—a material pair that works well in one topology may fail in another. Literature L04, L06, L10, L13, and L19 motivate UV bandpass filter structures but do not certify any specific design. All routes respect the 30-layer maximum, no-metal constraint, and fused silica substrate requirement.

routes.title: HfO2/SiO2 periodic Bragg stack with single defect cavity
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A standard quarter-wave Bragg reflector pair (HfO2/SiO2) with a single half-wave defect cavity can achieve high transmission in 255-280 nm while blocking 300-1100 nm within 30 layers.
routes.design_principle: Bragg reflectors create high reflectance outside the passband through constructive interference of reflections from periodic high/low index interfaces. A defect layer in the center creates a transmission resonance within the stopband.
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 15 layers (7 pairs + 1 cavity + 7 pairs)
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count is 15, well under 30-layer limit
HfO2 and SiO2 are conventional e-beam or ion-assisted depositable materials
No metal layers
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory for Bragg reflectors
Defect mode theory for cavity resonance
Transfer matrix method for multilayer calculation
expected_advantages: Well-understood design topology
HfO2/SiO2 pair has good UV transparency down to ~250 nm
Single cavity simplifies optimization
known_risks: HfO2 may have increased absorption below 260 nm
Single cavity may not provide sharp enough passband edges
Blocking bandwidth may be insufficient for 300-1100 nm range

Optimize all individual layer thicknesses to maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm while minimizing transmittance in 300-700 nm and 700-1100 nm. No metal layers. Materials: hfo2, SiO2 (Gao).

routes.scientific_hypothesis: Al2O3/MgF2 material pair provides better UV transparency than HfO2/SiO2 for 255-280 nm bandpass, achieving higher transmission with comparable blocking performance.
routes.design_principle: MgF2 has exceptional UV transparency down to 200 nm and lower refractive index than SiO2. Al2O3 also maintains good UV transparency. The lower index contrast may require more layers but reduces absorption risk.

routes.scientific_hypothesis: A chirped period distribution in the Bragg reflector sections broadens the blocking bandwidth to cover 300-1100 nm more effectively than uniform quarter-wave stacks.
routes.design_principle: Chirping the layer thicknesses (varying the period across the stack) creates multiple overlapping stopbands that merge into a broader blocking region. This addresses the challenge of blocking both visible and NIR with one structure.

research_influence: L04 (solar-blind bandpass filters) motivated the defect-cavity topology in routes 01, 02, and 04
L06 (broadband blocking bandpass filters) motivated the chirped stack in route 03 and the high-layer-count approach in route 06
L10 and L13 (UV coatings and solar-blind filters) provided general motivation for all UV bandpass routes
L19 (linear variable UV filters) supported the chirped topology hypothesis in route 03
L25 (UV dielectric coating damage) informed material selection considerations for Al2O3 and HfO2 in routes 02 and 05
L17 (titania/silica tri-layer) motivated the three-material approach in route 05
L37 (low stress coatings) informed the stress considerations in route 06
unresolved_decisions: Angle of incidence was not specified in the request; all routes assume normal incidence (0 degrees) as a baseline hypothesis
Polarization state was not specified; all routes assume unpolarized light or treat TE and TM equally at normal incidence
Specific deposition method (e-beam, ion-assisted, sputtering) not specified; routes assume conventional depositable materials without process-specific constraints
plan.stop_if_all_routes_fail: If all six routes fail to achieve best_target_score above 0.3 after full optimization, the problem may require non-planar structures, metal-dielectric hybrids, or relaxation of the 30-layer constraint. Return to problem formulation stage.

selector_prompt.system:
You are the internal material-dataset selector inside a scientific TMM
harness. This is not route planning and you must not redesign the route.
Return exactly one JSON object and no markdown:
{"selections":[{"request_id":"material_01","selected_rank":1,"provider":"rii_sqlite","dataset_id":562,"reason":"..."}]}

The user question is authoritative. Each request contains candidates already
retrieved from the local MaterialRegistry and sorted by three equal physical
metrics: target-band coverage, n/k completeness, and sampling density. Rank 1
is the most physically reliable candidate; lower rank means less reliable.
Choose exactly one candidate from the supplied list for every request. Never
invent, rename, or edit a provider or dataset_id. The selected_rank must point
to the selected array element, and provider/dataset_id must copy that element.

Material identity, stoichiometry, explicit material state/preparation, and an
explicit requested source are hard constraints. A candidate with
formula_exact=false or semantic_match=same_element_family is not an allowed
substitute for a formula request. SiO is not SiO2, even if the SiO2 candidate
has better physical coverage. When several candidates satisfy the hard
constraints, select the highest-ranked one (usually rank 1). If no candidate
satisfies them, return selected_rank:null, provider:null, dataset_id:null and
reason:"needs_confirmation" for that request.

plan.planning_summary: This control axis tests whether a recalled Fabry-Perot cavity bandpass design pattern, using HfO2/MgF2 material pairs, can achieve the required UV transmission with visible/NIR suppression. The design draws on prior knowledge of UV bandpass filter architecture without consulting any literature. I would have wanted to look up actual extinction coefficients for these materials at 255-280 nm to confirm absorption losses, and to verify the optimal cavity count for this specific bandwidth.

routes.title: HfO2-MgF2 Fabry-Perot Cavity Bandpass Filter for Solar-Blind UV
routes.scientific_hypothesis: A symmetric Fabry-Perot cavity design with HfO2/MgF2 distributed Bragg reflectors can achieve high transmittance in 255-280 nm while suppressing 300-1100 nm, with performance improving as cavity thickness is tuned.
routes.design_principle: Recalled knowledge: Bandpass filters use high/low index pairs to create reflector stacks, with a cavity layer between them creating a transmission peak at the design wavelength. Quarter-wave optical thickness at center wavelength creates constructive interference in the passband. MgF2 has low UV absorption; HfO2 provides sufficient index contrast.
routes.proposed_topology: Air | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | MgF2 | HfO2 | SiO2 substrate
design_variables: Individual layer thicknesses for all 29 layers (nm)
soft_objectives: Maximize mean transmittance in 255-280 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 300-700 nm band
Minimize mean transmittance in 700-1100 nm band
Keep total layer count at exactly 29 layers
manufacturing_considerations: Total layer count fixed at 29 (under 30 limit)
No metal layers used
All materials are conventional depositable inorganic dielectrics
Layer thicknesses should remain in practical deposition range (20-200 nm typical)
theory_basis: Recalled: Fabry-Perot cavity filters use two reflector stacks separated by a spacer layer to create a transmission band
Recalled: Quarter-wave optical thickness (n*d = lambda/4) at center wavelength maximizes reflector performance
Recalled: MgF2 has good transmission down to ~120 nm UV range
Recalled: HfO2 provides index contrast ~2.0-2.1 in UV versus MgF2 ~1.4
Recalled: More reflector pairs increase bandwidth selectivity but add layers
Recalled: Symmetric cavity designs reduce sidelobes in the stopband
expected_advantages: HfO2/MgF2 pair is commonly used for UV coatings from recalled knowledge
29 layers provides sufficient reflector pairs for good blocking
Cavity design naturally creates the required bandpass behavior
All materials are in the guaranteed resolution list
known_risks: Uncertain whether HfO2 has acceptable absorption at 255-280 nm - would need to check extinction coefficient data
Uncertain whether 29 layers is optimal versus fewer layers with different topology - this is a recalled rule of thumb
Uncertain about the exact index values at UV wavelengths - using recalled approximate values
Angle of incidence not specified in request - assuming normal incidence, but space platform may have off-axis rays
Polarization effects not addressed - may matter for oblique incidence in orbit
Would need to verify MgF2 stress properties for space environment qualification
routes.execution_request_english: Design a 29-layer planar multilayer filter coating on fused silica (SiO2 (Gao)) substrate with air incidence. Use only hfo2 and MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos) as coating materials in the following fixed sequence from air side: HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2, MgF2 (Rodriguez-de_Marcos), HfO2. Optimize all 29 layer thicknesses as independent variables. Target: maximize transmittance in 255-280 nm wavelength band, minimize transmittance in 300-700 nm band, minimize transmittance in 700-1100 nm band. Normal incidence, unpolarized light. No metal layers. Total layer count fixed at 29.
